focus: traceability — plugin versus core parity: workspace resolution and packet-read fields

findingDetails.title: Plugin still resolves a packet against the directory it was handed, so a bind from a subdirectory fails where the core succeeds
findingDetails.evidence: The plugin takes `workspace = options.directory || process.cwd()` and hands it straight to the shared reader (opencode-goal.js:1817-1818), stores that raw directory as the record's workspace (:1838), and resolves the packet against it on every later render (resolvePacketGoalForRecord, :2701-2704). The core resolves through goalScope.workspace (goal-core.cjs:191), which comes from resolveRepoRoot walking up to .git or .opencode/skills (:135-144). Reproduced on a fixture packet with both writers given scratch/ws/sub: core returned ok with the repo root stored, the plugin raised PACKET_GOAL_NOT_FOUND; from the workspace root both stored identical pointers. Pass-1 F013 was closed by deleting the dead ternary; the root walk was never added, so the fix is incomplete.
findingDetails.impact: On the primary runtime a bind issued from a narrower directory fails, and a record carrying a narrower workspace keeps failing at render time so the injection disappears while the record still reads active.
findingDetails.recommendation: Resolve the workspace through the same repo-root walk the core uses, or refuse a non-root directory with an explicit error. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both bind paths, the stored pointer, the later render resolution and the record walk read directly; reproduced against the plugin's pinned __test seam and the core on the same fixture.

findingDetails.title: Plugin packet action omits the budget field its CLI twin prints
findingDetails.evidence: The plugin's session-free packet action returns packet_path, packet_nested, packet_durable_chars, packet_slice_hash, objective_slice and chat_slice (opencode-goal.js:2989-2995) with no packet_budget, while the core CLI prints the same block plus `packet_budget=${packet.budgetState}` (bin/goal.cjs:211) and the plugin's own bind reports the budget (opencode-goal.js:2974-2977). The reader computes budgetState for both (goal-slice.cjs:224-226). Probe output confirmed: packet_durable_chars=188 and no budget line from the plugin.
findingDetails.impact: The pre-bind read reports the size but not the tier the validator will apply, and the two runtimes return different field sets for one action.
findingDetails.recommendation: Emit packet_budget from the plugin's packet action, as its bind already does. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both packet actions and the plugin's bind output read directly; plugin output observed through the pinned test seam.

results.summary: Pi, Cursor and Devin inherit the core's repo-root walk; the OpenCode plugin does not, and its packet read omits the budget field the CLI prints.
